core_job: For a person who cooks at home most weeknights for 1 to 4 people: keep an honest kitchen list with use-by dates, and every evening answer "what should I cook tonight", ranked by what needs using first. When they cook, the list updates itself. All on the device, offline, with no account. Today the app only checks whether an ingredient is present, never looks at use-by dates, has 12 recipes and no way to edit an item (verified: lib/domain/recipe_matcher.dart:4-10, lib/domain/catalogue.dart, lib/main.dart:1758). Baseline measured today: analyze clean, 134 tests pass.
signature: "Use It Up". (1) Recipes ranked by a rescue score: held ingredients weighted by days left (today 5, 1 day 4, 2 days 3, 3 days 2, 4-7 days 1; expired 0 and flagged "check it first"), and each card shows the at-risk items it uses. (2) "Cook with a swap": a bundled substitution table written in-house, at most one swap per recipe. (3) "I cooked this" deducts the recipe's structured amounts from the kitchen, converting units only within a fixed table and never guessing. (4) Removing an item asks Used it / Binned it / Just remove, which feeds a monthly tally of the user's own counts. All Dart on the device; no API, Supabase or keys. Competitors were checked through the keyless iTunes Lookup API (their own App Store descriptions, not hands-on tests): SuperCook (id1477747816) matches recipes to what you have but describes no use-by tracking; NoWaste (id926211004) and FridgeBuddy (id1500190823) track expiry but describe no ranking of recipes by what expires first. TheMealDB was rejected because its terms require a paid supporter key for app-store release (curl of its api.php).
